hero.headline: Treasury moves to cut off crypto exchange MEXC from U.S. financial system over alleged $16 billion in illicit transactions
hero.teaser: The U.S. Treasury Department moved to cut off cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over allegations the platform processed $16 billion in illicit transac
hero.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department moved to cut off cryptocurrency exchange MEXC from the American financial system over allegations the platform processed $16 billion in illicit transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia. The action targets MEXC Global for alleged sanctions violations.

The Treasury decision blocks MEXC from accessing U.S. financial infrastructure and conducting transactions with American counterparties. The enforcement measure represents one of the largest actions against a cryptocurrency exchange based on alleged illicit transaction volume.

The alleged $16 billion in flows involve transactions connected to sanctioned countries including Iran, North Korea and Russia. The Treasury did not specify the time period over which the transactions allegedly occurred or detail the nature of the illicit activity.

In response to the Treasury action, digital asset company NatGold Digital announced it would immediately delist its NATG token from MEXC. The move reflects the immediate market consequences for platforms cut off from the U.S. financial system.

cards.headline: Congress demands answers on Nvidia CEO's reported ties to alleged Chinese spy
cards.teaser: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged an investigation, while a group of House Republican committee chairs requested a briefing from Huang by November 11 to determine whether U.S. national security has been compromised.

Multiple news outlets reported Friday that Alice Huang, a tech executive with whom Jensen Huang had contact, was recruited by Chinese intelligence officials to influence the Nvidia CEO's position on U.S. chip export policy toward China. The New York Times and Financial Times reported she was specifically tasked with convincing him to lobby U.S. officials to allow exports of advanced chips to China. The Financial Times also reported that the two had a romantic relationship.

Nvidia has denied that Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang was anything beyond a typical business contact and said no sensitive information was shared. The Chinese government has also denied involvement. The company did not respond to a request for comment Saturday.

The House Republican chairs who requested the briefing asked Huang to explain his relationship with Alice Huang and detail Nvidia's controls over sensitive information. Nvidia produces chips central to advanced artificial intelligence development, a technology priority for the Trump administration as it seeks to maintain a competitive edge over China. Reports indicate Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies despite export restrictions.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

cards.headline: Stocks plunge into correction after brief post-midterm rally as AI regulation fears hit tech
cards.body:
Wall Street reversed from celebration to selloff within 24 hours this week after midterm election results, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite entering correction territory amid concerns about artificial intelligence regulation. The Dow surged more than 1,500 points Wednesday following a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress, while the S&P 500 rallied nearly 2 percent. By Thursday, stocks had reversed course as investors sold AI and chip stocks.

The market volatility index, the VIX, spiked to its highest level since late March, when President Donald Trump extended a deadline related to the Iran war. The swing marked the latest in a year of sharp reversals for markets.

The Democratic victories introduced uncertainty for the artificial intelligence industry. Newly elected governors in states accounting for an estimated 45 percent of planned U.S. data center capacity have promised to stop or pause data center construction, according to Goldman Sachs. In Texas, where more than half of the country's planned data center capacity is slated for construction, Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race after pledging a moratorium on new data center approvals.

Wednesday's rally appeared driven by investors welcoming the removal of election uncertainty and the prospect of divided government potentially limiting some of Trump's agenda. Falling oil prices also eased inflation concerns. Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, said the drop in volatility may have encouraged volatility-sensitive trading strategies to buy stocks, adding upward pressure to the rally before the subsequent reversal.

hero.headline: Israeli President Herzog tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government after inconclusive election
hero.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government, giving the former military chief 28 days to build an administration after last week's election produced no clear majority. Herzog announced the decision after consulting with political parties represented in the incoming Knesset, Israel's parliament. Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership compared to 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The election left Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies with 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48 seats. Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, won 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters, positioning them as potential power brokers.

Eisenkot now faces the challenge of assembling a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Three paths appear possible: a national unity government involving both Eisenkot and Netanyahu, a right-wing coalition built on defections from Eisenkot's bloc to Netanyahu, or an Eisenkot-led government relying on the Arab parties. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the election not to work with Arab parties to form a government, though observers have speculated an agreement could be reached.

No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, requiring all governments to be coalitions. Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five separate elections as Netanyahu and his rivals repeatedly failed to form stable coalitions. Herzog said during his consultations that preventing another election round would require parties to recognize that not every campaign commitment could be fulfilled in the current reality.

cards.headline: Russian strikes wound nine, cut power and water in Kyiv ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
cards.teaser: Drone and missile attacks hit Ukraine days before scheduled negotiations with Russia and the United States.
cards.body:
Russian drone and missile attacks wounded nine people in Ukraine and caused power and water outages in Kyiv, according to Ukrainian authorities. The strikes targeted Ukraine's energy infrastructure in an overnight assault.

The attacks occurred days before scheduled talks involving Ukraine, Russia, and the United States in Abu Dhabi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that four out of 36 missiles were shot down and said Russia used North Korean weapons in the assault.

cards.headline: Pope Leo XIV urges Uruguayans to build bridges, champions universal healthcare during South America tour
cards.teaser: The pontiff celebrated Mass in Uruguay as part of a 12-day, three-country tour following his lung cancer surgery.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass in Uruguay, urging the faithful to act as bridge builders of fraternity and faith. During his visit, the pontiff championed universal healthcare in a speech delivered weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery.

The Uruguay stop is part of a 12-day, three-country South America tour. The pope also praised the local mate tea ritual and called on Uruguayans not to turn away from injustice.

cards.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
cards.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.

Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

cards.headline: Gunman kills six in attack on Krakow's main square, three more bodies found at his home
cards.teaser: At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday afternoon, and police later found three bodies at his home. The a
cards.body:
At least six people were killed and several others injured when a gunman opened fire in central Krakow on Saturday afternoon, and police later found three bodies at his home. The a

The attacker, identified as a 25-year-old Polish man, drove into Krakow's Main Market Square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car. Armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes, preventing further casualties.

hero.headline: Wisconsin state trooper detained by ICE released under supervision after intervention by DHS secretary
hero.teaser: A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air
hero.body:
A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an airport Thursday while attempting to visit his parents. Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney.

Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher. His parents applied for asylum, and Van Der Merwe was granted work authorization while that process proceeded. He later attended the New Mexico Military Institute and sought to serve in the U.S. military but was not permitted because of his immigration status. Van Der Merwe began working as a Wisconsin state trooper in July 2025 and remains authorized to work in the country, Christopher said.

The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that Van Der Merwe had legal permission to remain in the United States until September 2019 but overstayed his admission. The agency characterized the overstay as defiance of federal immigration law.

Christopher said the case was egregious and that he could not identify any public benefit from detaining Van Der Merwe. The trooper will remain under an order of supervision, with specific conditions to be determined within two weeks, according to his attorney.

cards.headline: Six killed in shooting in Krakow, Poland; British citizen among dead
cards.teaser: A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo
cards.body:
A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo

A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

cards.headline: Hamilton and Verstappen to start from back of grid at São Paulo Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix after power-unit changes resulted in penalties for both
cards.body:
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix after power-unit changes resulted in penalties for both

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also face grid penalties, with Leclerc dropping 10 places and Russell five. Hamilton initially faced a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season.

cards.headline: Anthropic IPO faces headwinds as AI data center backlash grows
cards.teaser: The AI company disclosed $895 billion in infrastructure commitments as public opposition to data centers intensifies.
cards.body:
Anthropic disclosed in an amended IPO prospectus this week that it has entered purchase commitments and lease agreements totaling about $895.4 billion, substantially all for compute and infrastructure. The company said opposition to data center development has become more organized across jurisdictions, and its public profile could draw particular scrutiny to associated projects.

Americans concerned about inflation and high gas prices have grown worried the facilities could worsen environmental harms, raise utility bills, and contribute to job loss. Anthropic noted in its risk factors that proposed data centers have become a physical manifestation of widespread antipathy toward AI.

cards.headline: Musk says SpaceX could acquire legacy telecom carrier to use spectrum more efficiently
cards.teaser: Deutsche Telekom CEO estimates entry cost at $220 billion as SpaceX eyes industry expansion.
cards.body:
Elon Musk told investors on November 6 that SpaceX could buy a legacy telecom carrier and use its spectrum "ten times more effectively," though he named no target and made any purchase conditional on improved efficiency. The comment came during a video appearance at the Baron Investment Conference in New York. SpaceX shares rose 8.62% to $134.27, while Verizon and AT&T each slipped 0.89%.

Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Hoettges said on his company's November 5 earnings call that SpaceX would need at least 200 billion euros, roughly $220 billion, to compete with established U.S. carriers. He cited SpaceX's 76 megahertz of spectrum compared with T-Mobile's roughly 400 megahertz, and estimated tower leasing alone would cost $20 billion to $30 billion.

cards.teaser: Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the
cards.body:
Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck vehicles at its Texas factory next year, Elon Musk said Friday. Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the

Musk did not specify whether the company plans to stop making the trucks entirely or shift production elsewhere, but said the decision was to make room for building more of its self-driving Cybercab cars. Wes Morrill, the project's lead engineer, wrote on social media that Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab, appearing to suggest the vehicle is being discontinued.

cards.headline: Wave of bomb threats and cyberattacks across Europe raises questions about coordination
cards.teaser: A series of bomb threats targeting airlines and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure across Europe has disrupted everyday life and heightened security concerns, though the perpe
cards.body:
A series of bomb threats targeting airlines and cyberattacks on critical infrastructure across Europe has disrupted everyday life and heightened security concerns, though the perpe

The incidents have affected multiple sectors, including aviation, healthcare, and food supply systems. Cyberattacks targeted European refrigeration systems and critical health infrastructure, including a French blood bank.

hero.headline: U.S. intelligence memo claimed Chinese officials recruited tech executive to spy on Nvidia CEO
hero.body:
A U.S. intelligence memo circulated earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The New York Times first reported on the memo, which was based on U.S. intelligence.

The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang. An Nvidia spokesperson told the Times that Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were not unusual and that the company does not share classified information with its customers.

A separate Times report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company that the U.S. Commerce Department had authorized to buy advanced Nvidia chips. When reporters visited the office address listed by New Matrix, they found only a hollow gray shell, raising concerns that the company could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm.

The Nvidia spokesperson said the company sells the first, best and most of its technology in America. Nvidia manufactures graphics processing units that are critical for artificial intelligence development and are subject to U.S. export controls aimed at limiting China's access to advanced chips.

cards.headline: OpenAI revises data center policies after Democratic midterm gains
cards.teaser: Company ends NDA requirements and promises more transparency following Democratic victories in states and local ballot measures restricting data center development.
cards.body:
OpenAI released a new compute campus policy blueprint ending nondisclosure agreement requirements for officials and promising greater project transparency, following Democratic gains in this week's midterm elections. Voters in dozens of local ballot measures rejected or restricted data center development, and Democratic candidates including Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on promises to limit data center expansion.

The policy shift follows criticism that companies pursued data center approvals secretively, particularly in water-scarce regions. OpenAI is rebranding the facilities as compute campuses, though industry observers question whether the terminology change will influence public perception or regulatory outcomes.

hero.headline: Notre Dame defeats Miami 24-17 in matchup of top-ranked teams
hero.body:
Notre Dame defeated Miami 24-17 on Saturday night in South Bend, Indiana, handing the top-ranked Hurricanes their first loss of the season. The Fighting Irish, ranked 11th in the College Football Playoff committee rankings despite being fourth in the Associated Press poll, secured a crucial victory in what had become a must-win game for their playoff hopes.

Quarterback CJ Carr threw three touchdown passes for Notre Dame, including two to Micah Gilbert. Gilbert's 20-yard touchdown reception gave the Irish a 24-3 lead in the third quarter. Carr also connected with Jordan Faison on a 27-yard touchdown pass in which Faison made a back-shoulder catch and tapped his toes in bounds. Carr capped a two-minute drive before halftime with an 18-yard touchdown strike to Gilbert.

Miami struggled offensively without star receiver Malachi Toney, who was out with an ankle injury suffered in practice. The Hurricanes, who entered the game averaging nearly 48 points per game, managed only three points in the first half. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah threw touchdown passes to Cooper Barkate and Elija Lofton in the second half, with Lofton making an impressive toe-tapping catch in the end zone. However, the Hurricanes could not overcome the deficit.

Notre Dame's defense pressured Mensah throughout the game, with Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa recording a crucial third-down sack in the second half. Jordan Faison also returned a punt 55 yards to the Miami 30-yard line. The Irish controlled the game after building their 21-point lead, withstanding Miami's late comeback attempt to secure the victory.

cards.headline: NFL's Player Personnel Handbook gives league wide discretion over Brandon Aiyuk's reinstatement
cards.teaser: League language implies commissioner has broad authority to approve reinstatement from reserve/left squad list, tying Aiyuk's return to financial dispute with 49ers.
cards.body:
The NFL's Player Personnel Handbook grants the commissioner apparently unlimited discretion over reinstatement requests from the reserve/left squad list, according to league interpretation in Brandon Aiyuk's case. The handbook requires players to apply for reinstatement but does not explicitly limit the commissioner's approval authority. The league has delayed action on Aiyuk's application since October 27.

The 49ers are seeking reimbursement of up to $13 million in previously paid bonus money from Aiyuk, and the league appears to be tying his reinstatement to resolution of that financial dispute. The NFL Players Association has remained silent, potentially because the Collective Bargaining Agreement contains no specific provisions governing the reserve/left squad list, leaving the matter within management rights.

cards.headline: Chev Clarke scores seventh-round stoppage upset over former cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith
cards.teaser: Billam-Smith suffers first career stoppage loss in all-British non-title fight at London's Copper Box arena.
cards.body:
Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career Saturday as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight. Clarke landed a right hand early in the seventh round that floored Billam-Smith, who rose but was knocked down again moments later. The referee stopped the contest after Clarke connected with two more blows, despite immediate protest from Billam-Smith.

Clarke improved to 13-2 and inflicted a third professional defeat on Billam-Smith, who previously lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019. Clarke had also defeated Billam-Smith in the amateur ranks a decade ago.

cards.headline: Norris takes pole for third straight year in Brazil as rain shuffles grid
cards.teaser: Lando Norris secured pole position at the rain-soaked Sao Paulo Grand Prix for the third consecutive year, while Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen will start from the back due to engine penalties.
cards.body:
Lando Norris claimed pole position at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix for the third consecutive year after qualifying was delayed nearly 90 minutes due to dangerous wet conditions. The McLaren driver said the session brought some of the wettest conditions he had ever experienced and expressed hope for more rain in Sunday's race.

Grid penalties for engine changes dropped Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen to 20th and 21st on the starting grid. The shuffled order elevated Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg to the second row, while Mercedes' George Russell qualified second but will start fifth due to his own penalty.

cards.headline: Thick fog obscured live FA Cup broadcast as commentators struggled to see play
cards.teaser: BBC commentators and managers were unable to see much of the action during Altrincham's first-round match against Notts County.
cards.body:
Thick fog at Altrincham's Moss Lane ground left BBC commentators unable to see most of the action during a live FA Cup first-round match between Altrincham and Notts County on Saturday. Commentator Steve Bower said that after the 60th minute, he could not see which team had the ball once play moved beyond the center circle, calling the conditions the worst in his 35-year career.

Notts County won on penalties after the match went to extra-time following a 2-2 draw. Managers on the touchline also struggled to assess tactics, and players told Bower they could not see both goals or corner flags from midfield. The match was nearly called off due to visibility issues.

cards.headline: LSU loses to Alabama 31-13 as Lane Kiffin falls to 0-3 against ranked opponents
cards.teaser: The Tigers surrendered 21 unanswered points after taking a third-quarter lead, extending Kiffin's losing streak against Alabama to six games.
cards.body:
Louisiana State University lost to fifth-ranked Alabama 31-13 on Saturday, dropping to 6-3 overall and 0-3 against teams in the College Football Playoff rankings. After taking a 13-10 lead in the third quarter, the Tigers allowed 21 unanswered points. The loss extended coach Lane Kiffin's losing streak against Alabama to six consecutive games.

Kiffin, who signed a seven-year, $91 million contract and assembled a roster valued near $50 million according to 247Sports, has defeated unranked opponents but struggled against elite competition. LSU turned the ball over twice, failed to convert on downs three times, and managed just one field goal after reaching first-and-goal against Alabama's defense.

cards.headline: Willy Hutchinson upsets Joshua Buatsi to win WBC light-heavyweight title in Manchester rematch
cards.teaser: Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rema
cards.body:
Willy Hutchinson won the WBC light-heavyweight championship Saturday night in Manchester, defeating Joshua Buatsi by decision to avenge a loss from 2024. The judges scored the rema

The judges scored the rematch 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 in favor of Hutchinson, making the 28-year-old Scot the first British champion at the weight since Nathan Cleverly in 2017. The bout was elevated from an interim title fight to a full championship after American David Benavidez vacated the belt to move up to cruiserweight.

hero.headline: Stephen Colbert and Yo-Yo Ma's Harvard event cut short by fire alarm amid graduate student union strike
hero.body:
Stephen Colbert and cellist Yo-Yo Ma were rushed out of a Harvard University event Thursday after a fire alarm was pulled during their appearance, which had drawn hundreds of union protesters outside who objected to the pair crossing their picket line. The Harvard Graduate Student Union had urged both performers to cancel the talk in solidarity with their strike, which began October 27. Despite the protests and chanting outside the venue that made it difficult to hear the speakers, Colbert and Ma proceeded with the event.

The fire alarm forced organizers to end the event during the question-and-answer portion and escort Colbert out of the building. The union denied responsibility for the alarm, stating in a social media post that it was unrelated to their picketing activity and that members were relieved no one inside was at risk.

The union had sent multiple formal communications to Colbert and Ma's teams in advance, requesting they move the event off-site or virtually, reschedule, or cancel to avoid crossing the picket line. Representatives from Colbert's union, SAG-AFTRA, and Ma's union, the Boston Musicians Association, also reached out on the graduate union's behalf with the same request. The union said Colbert and Ma refused to speak with union members as they left and continued the event without regard for the picket line.

The graduate student union has been on strike demanding a contract that includes wage increases and protections for non-citizens and against harassment and discrimination. Graduate classes have gone untaught since the strike began. Author John Green moved his own Harvard event to accommodate the strike, calling it an easy decision and donating his proceeds to the union.

cards.headline: Hockey romance series Heated Rivalry films two seasons and holiday movie back-to-back
cards.teaser: The show's theatrical release drew strong opening-weekend box office as production advances on multiple projects.
cards.body:
Heated Rivalry is filming seasons two and three back-to-back, wrapping production in late November or early December before shooting a standalone holiday film in December, according to sources. The Christmas-themed movie, centered on characters Scott and Kip rather than leads Ilya and Shane, is planned for theatrical release next December.

The series' six-episode first season is currently screening at Regal Cinema, AMC, and Cinemark locations in paired-episode showings. The theatrical run collected $420,000 on Friday and is tracking toward a $1.3 million opening weekend across 880 theaters. Season two is confirmed to premiere in spring 2027.

cards.headline: Bill Skarsgård says he was not considered for new James Bond role but would play a villain
cards.teaser: The Swedish actor said he was not asked to test for Denis Villeneuve's Bond reboot but would be interested in a one-off villain part.
cards.body:
Bill Skarsgård said he was not asked to audition for the new James Bond role in Denis Villeneuve's upcoming reboot. In a podcast appearance, the Swedish actor joked that casting directors may have passed over him for being Swedish, noting he "wasn't even thrown into the mix" while British and Australian actors were considered. Recent screen tests have reportedly included Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult.

Skarsgård said he would not want to commit to a decade-plus Bond contract but would be interested in playing a one-off villain, comparing the role to Mads Mikkelsen's Bond antagonist. The actor, known for villainous parts in "It," "Nosferatu," and "John Wick: Chapter 4," said he is becoming more selective about villain roles and seeks only original characters he has not played before.

cards.headline: Pokemon anime studio unveils AI coloring tool trained on three hand-painted frames
cards.teaser: OLM developed the system under a Japanese government-backed research project, cutting painting workload by around 30%.
cards.body:
OLM, the Japanese animation studio behind the Pokemon anime series, has developed an AI coloring tool that learns a show's visual style from just three hand-painted frames, board director Yotsukura Tatsuo said at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest in Taipei. The tool emerged from ANIMINS, a 15-month research project under GENIAC, a generative AI program overseen by Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry that concluded in February.

An artist colors three frames by hand, and the system learns the line shapes and color palette in about 90 seconds, then colors each remaining frame in around 15 seconds. At proof-of-concept stage, Yotsukura estimated the tool has cut painting workload by around 30 percent.

cards.headline: AI Could Make Filmmaking Costlier Than 35mm Era, Korean Production Pioneers Warn
cards.teaser: Rising token costs could push AI feature budgets above traditional film costs unless studios minimize revision rounds, industry leaders told Taiwan Creative Content Fest.
cards.body:
Rising token costs could push AI feature budgets above traditional film costs unless studios minimize revision rounds, industry leaders told Taiwan Creative Content Fest.

Kim Kwang-jib, founder of AI content studio Studio Meta-K, told Taiwan Creative Content Fest that token costs for a 100-minute film using premium commercial AI tools currently reach 500 million won ($366,000), but could jump tenfold if AI companies raise prices. That would exceed typical Korean and Taiwanese live-action budgets of 3 billion to 5 billion won ($2.2 million to $3.66 million).

cards.headline: Kirby Howell-Baptiste discusses scene-stealing role in Jordan Firstman's 'Club Kid'
cards.teaser: The British actor describes her character Edison as a tornado who upends the protagonist's life.
cards.body:
Kirby Howell-Baptiste plays Edison, a chaotic party girl in Jordan Firstman's comedy drama "Club Kid." In a pivotal apartment scene, Edison delivers shocking news in an insensitive manner while offering cocaine to protagonist Peter, then leaves a child named Arlo in his care and fails to return.

Howell-Baptiste describes Edison as "a complete tornado" and an amalgamation of party people Firstman has encountered. Though the character disappears after the apartment scene, Peter's subsequent search across New York house parties reveals Edison was kicked out of multiple venues for her unmanageable behavior.

cards.headline: 'Little Rascals' actor Brandon 'Bug' Hall seeks financial help before sixth child
cards.teaser: The former child star, known for playing Alfalfa, asked for assistance as he prepares to welcome another baby.
cards.body:
Brandon "Bug" Hall, who played Alfalfa in the 1994 film "The Little Rascals," has publicly asked for financial help as he prepares to welcome his sixth child. The former child actor indicated that times have been difficult.

Hall gained fame as a child star in the popular family comedy but has largely remained out of the spotlight in recent years. Details about his current circumstances or the nature of his financial appeal were not specified in available reports.

hero.headline: Congress demands answers on Nvidia CEO's reported ties to alleged Chinese spy
hero.teaser: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged
hero.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing congressional scrutiny after reports surfaced that he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Sen. Chris Coons pledged an investigation, while a group of House Republican committee chairs requested a briefing from Huang by November 11 to determine whether U.S. national security has been compromised.

Multiple news outlets reported Friday that Alice Huang, a tech executive with whom Jensen Huang had contact, was recruited by Chinese intelligence officials to influence the Nvidia CEO's position on U.S. chip export policy toward China. The New York Times and Financial Times reported she was specifically tasked with convincing him to lobby U.S. officials to allow exports of advanced chips to China. The Financial Times also reported that the two had a romantic relationship.

Nvidia has denied that Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang was anything beyond a typical business contact and said no sensitive information was shared. The Chinese government has also denied involvement. The company did not respond to a request for comment Saturday.

The House Republican chairs who requested the briefing asked Huang to explain his relationship with Alice Huang and detail Nvidia's controls over sensitive information. Nvidia produces chips central to advanced artificial intelligence development, a technology priority for the Trump administration as it seeks to maintain a competitive edge over China. Reports indicate Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies despite export restrictions.

cards.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'

Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night after Trump blamed her for the election results in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump will install Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, in the position starting Monday.
